what: Life Time runs large athletic clubs in the United States and Canada: not gyms but resorts with pools, tennis and pickleball courts, cafes, spas and co-working space, at premium membership prices.
customers: Affluent households paying well above a typical gym membership, often for the whole family.
money: personal training, spa, cafe and programmes
moat: Clubs that cost tens of millions each to build, on land in wealthy suburbs, which a competitor cannot replicate quickly and which members treat as a daily habit.
risks: $4.1B of debt against $205M of cash, and free cash flow is negative because of club construction
A recession would test whether a premium membership is kept or cancelled
Each new club takes years to reach full membership, so growth consumes cash first
opportunities: Revenue grew from $1.3B to $3.0B in four years with a 12.5% net margin
Analysts see about 24% upside, with 15 covering the stock
Revenue per member keeps rising as members buy training, spa and programmes on top of dues
watch: Same-club revenue growth and the number of new clubs opened per year.
